title: identity.audit.archive.v1
description: The payload of an audit-archive event, derived from OutboxEventType::audit_archive_v1(). The event_type name is the version; the payload shape is owned by that version. No Rust type carries this payload today — only the event_type string exists — so this is a PROMISE for the producer that Phase 7 builds.
x-rust-type: NONE — the event_type string exists (OutboxEventType::audit_archive_v1); no payload struct exists
x-serde-status: the event_type is IMPLEMENTED; the payload is NOT. A producer that writes this payload does not exist yet.

window_start_ms.description: Inclusive start of the archive window, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

window_end_ms.description: Exclusive end of the archive window, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
window_end_ms.x-why-exclusive: An exclusive end is what makes two consecutive windows partition a timeline without an off-by-one at every boundary. A closed interval would double-archive or drop one row at every window edge.

row_count.description: How many audit rows the window contained, when the producer knows it before writing the event.
row_count.x-not-logs: A count, not the rows. The event announces that a window was archived; it does not carry the rows themselves, which stay in the audit store where an operator can query them.

destination.description: Where the window was archived to, as an opaque storage reference. The producer's choice, not this contract's.

x-consumption.idempotency: keyed on QueuedEvent.id (the outbox event id), never on the payload. Two archive events for overlapping windows are two facts and must both be processed; the consumer decides whether the second is a no-op.
x-consumption.refusal: a consumer that cannot recognise the type refuses the message rather than guessing at the shape
x-consumption.disposition: BatchOutcome::Done, Retry, or DeadLetter — three named outcomes, no 'silently ignored'
x-consumption.ordering: not guaranteed. Archive events are independent windows and must not depend on arriving in order.
